text:
A 1,000 Wh station needs roughly **200 W of panels** to refill in about a day and a half of average sun, or **about 300 W** to refill in a single day.

**Estimate:** Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × efficiency factor). The efficiency factor usually falls between 0.7 and 0.75 to account for heat, angle, and controller losses.

| Panels | Time to refill (average ~4.5 peak sun hours) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 200 W | About 1.5 days | Matches the "divide Wh by 5" rule of thumb ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)) |
| ~300 W | About 1 day in summer | Based on 5 peak sun hours ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)) |
| ~735 W | About 1 day in northern winter | Based on 2 peak sun hours ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)) |

**Check these before buying:**
- **Station input limit:** Panels above the station's maximum solar input add nothing. A 1,000 Wh unit with a 200 W input cap can't use a 400 W panel. See [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge) for how limits work.
- **Voltage:** Panels wired in series add voltage, which can exceed the station's input window and damage it. Check the manual's range. [SolarNiverse](https://solarniverse.com/chargers/charge-power-station-with-solar-panels/) covers this.
- **Your sun hours:** Winter, cloudy areas, and northern latitudes can need several times more panel than the summer figure. [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station) gives typical peak sun hours by US city and season.

If you're also running devices while charging, the net charge rate is slower. Subtract the load from the solar input to get the real recharge speed.
